_comment: Hand-curated display names for OpenNGC rows whose 'Common names' column
carries more than one name. OpenNGC lists those names alphabetically, not
by usage, and parsers/deepsky.mjs used to keep the first — which handed M17
'Checkmark Nebula' over 'Swan', M42 'Great Orion Nebula' over 'Orion', and
M11 a French phrase over 'Wild Duck Cluster' (Jer, 2026-08-14).
Every upstream common name is now searchable regardless: the ones that are
not the display name are appended to `designations`. This file only decides
which one is the title, and adds names no source carries.
preferred: keyed by OpenNGC id. `name` becomes the row's display name. Only
list a row where the alphabetical first is the wrong title — a row absent
from here keeps OpenNGC's first name. A name NOT in the upstream list is
allowed (it then also enters `designations`), but say why in `note`.
parsers/deepsky.mjs FAILS LOUD on an entry whose id is not in the bake, or
whose id has no OpenNGC common name at all — both mean this file went stale.
extra_aliases: searchable names for rows where OpenNGC's list is incomplete
or oddly cased. Case-insensitive dedupe against the upstream names, and
these are added first, so listing 'Omega Nebula' here is also how the
upstream 'omega Nebula' spelling gets fixed for display.
named: titles for rows OpenNGC leaves unnamed. FAILS LOUD once OpenNGC
names the row — move it to `preferred` then.
rejected: upstream names that are wrong for the row. Dropped from the title
and from `designations`. FAILS LOUD once OpenNGC no longer carries the name.
Any name here (or upstream) makes the row a listed target: it skips the
magnitude ceiling, so naming a row is how a faint favourite gets in.

NGC6618.name: Swan Nebula
NGC6618.note: M17. Swan and Omega are the names in use; 'Checkmark' won only on the alphabet. Omega is the older name and rides along in extra_aliases.

NGC1976.name: Orion Nebula
NGC1976.note: M42. 'Great Orion Nebula' is the archaic long form.

NGC0650.name: Little Dumbbell Nebula
NGC0650.note: M76. Barbell and Cork are both in circulation but Little Dumbbell is the name it is catalogued under everywhere amateur.

NGC6705.name: Wild Duck Cluster
NGC6705.note: M11. OpenNGC's first entry is the French 'Amas de l'Ecu de Sobieski'.

NGC2070.name: Tarantula Nebula
NGC2070.note: '30 Dor Cluster' is the embedded cluster designation, not the nebula's popular name.

NGC0253.name: Sculptor Galaxy
NGC0253.note: Not in OpenNGC's list at all, which offers only 'Sculptor Filament' (a different, larger structure) and 'Silver Coin'. Sculptor Galaxy is the standard name; both upstream names stay searchable.

NGC2632.name: Beehive Cluster
NGC2632.note: M44. OpenNGC has the bare 'Beehive'; the cluster is universally 'Beehive Cluster'. 'Praesepe' stays searchable.

IC0443.name: Jellyfish Nebula
IC0443.note: OpenNGC's only name is 'Gem A', the radio-source label. Jellyfish is the name imagers use.

IC2602.name: Southern Pleiades
IC2602.note: C102. OpenNGC has only 'tet Car Cluster' (theta Carinae Cluster); Southern Pleiades is the popular name.

IC0063.name: Ghost of Cassiopeia
IC0063.note: The brighter, H-alpha half of the gamma Cas pair. Sh2-185 and LBN 622/623 resolve to this row.

IC0059.name: Ghost of Cassiopeia
IC0059.note: The fainter, reflection half of the same gamma Cas pair; both are imaged and labelled together.

NGC2024.name: Flame Nebula
NGC2024.note: OpenNGC puts 'Flame Nebula' on IC 434 instead (see rejected). NGC 2024 is the Flame.

IC0434.note: The Flame is NGC 2024. IC 434 is the emission strip the Horsehead (B 33) is silhouetted against.
